result.summary: Adds edge-case script and transaction test vectors to script_tests.json and tx_invalid.json. The new vectors cover interpreter corners including OP_CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY with -2, OP_IFDUP on negative zero, OP_ROLL with duplicate values, taproot output keys that are not valid x-coordinates, and single-flag STRICTENC, LOW_S, and NULLFAIL cases.
result.problem: Downstream and alternate implementations (such as bitcoin-s) that rely on Bitcoin Core's static test vectors can miss subtle script interpreter edge cases. Additionally, some policy validation cases were previously only caught when Bitcoin Core's C++ test harness injected flags dynamically, leaving consumers of the static JSON vectors without coverage.
evidence: Author note in PR description: "These were discovered by finding gaps in an alternate implementation (bitcoin-s)"
Author note in PR description: "Some policy cases were only caught by the tx_valid harness adding flags back, which implementations copying the JSON don't replicate."
result.card: Adds test vectors to script_tests.json and tx_invalid.json covering script interpreter edge cases such as OP_CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY with negative values, OP_IFDUP on negative zero, invalid Taproot public keys, and isolated policy flags. Downstream implementations that rely on Bitcoin Core's static JSON test vectors missed these corner cases because existing coverage partially depended on test harness flag injection. The edge cases were identified through coverage gaps found in an alternative Bitcoin implementation (bitcoin-s).

risk.why: Incorrect or invalid test vectors could cause test suite failures or mislead downstream implementations relying on the test vectors.
